title: helm(private): stabilize values schema and init hooks for upgrade/rollback compatibility
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped/VPC environments hit upgrade/rollback failures due to a) a stricter values.schema.json that rejected legacy installs and b) init hook behavior that left half-migrated secrets on failed upgrades. This PR stabilizes the private Helm chart by loosening the schema to be backward compatible, adding guarded init hooks for migration, and improving templating to support safe rollback.

What this change does:
- Add backward-compatible constraints to charts/private/values.schema.json so legacy installs without explicit new fields don't fail helm upgrade. The schema uses anyOf patterns and optional defaults where appropriate.
- Update charts/private/templates/init-migrate-secret-job.yaml to run as a pre-upgrade hook that safely migrates legacy secrets into the new secret format. The job is idempotent and has TTL and failurePolicy to avoid blocking.
- Add a post-upgrade hook charts/private/templates/post-upgrade-cleanup-job.yaml which cleans partially-created artifacts if a rollout fails and a rollback is triggered.
- Templating changes in charts/private/templates/_helpers.tpl to expose a single central annotation for controlling hook behavior (helm.redwood.ai/hook-safe), and add tolerations/affinity defaults for on-prem init jobs.
- Add tests/test-upgrade-rollback.yaml (helm test) to exercise upgrade->fail->rollback sequence in CI.
- Minor Chart.yaml and README.md updates to document the new values and migration behavior.

Compatibility notes:
- Default values are preserved; this change is intended to be non-breaking for current installs. However, cluster operators who explicitly relied on previous strict validation should review the loosened schema.

Checklist:
- [x] values.schema.json updated with compatibility rules
- [x] init/post-upgrade hooks implemented with safe guards
- [x] helm tests added and passing in CI
- [x] README and chart version bump

Related: ENG-8421 tracks the overall private upgrade stability effort. SUP-1213 captured the customer incident that motivated this work.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: The schema change caused a lint failure on CI initially because helm doesn't accept top-level anyOf in all versions. Can we ensure compatibility with helm v3.9+ and add a fallback?
Aisha Patel: Good catch - switched to property-level anyOf and added a compatibility note in Chart.yaml for supported helm versions. Pushed fix in 9a4f2b8.
Sofia Martinez: The init job looks good but we need to ensure the pod doesn't schedule on control-plane-only nodes in some on-prem clusters. Please add tolerations/affinity defaults.
Aisha Patel: Added tolerations/affinity defaults with opt-out via values (see _helpers.tpl change). Also added tests to validate toleration rendering.
Liam O'Connor: Please add an e2e helm test for upgrade->fail->rollback to avoid regressions in future. CI should run it with a short timeout.
Aisha Patel: Added tests/test-upgrade-rollback.yaml and wired it into chart-lint CI. Tests are lightweight and use a namespace-scoped failure to simulate partial migration.
Daniel Kim: Approved after CI passed and a small nit fixed in the README.
